traveler: Eugen Böhm Ritter von Bawerk (Eugen von Böhm-Bawerk)
title: The Agio on Present Goods: Böhm-Bawerk from Brünn to the Ehrengrab
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The House of Böhm at Brünn

stops.name: Brünn, a son to the Vizepräsident
stops.date_confidence: attested. The Austrian Biographical Dictionary gives 12.2.1851, Brünn. The parents come from Deutsche Biographie / NDB, which names Johann Karl Ritter Böhm von Bawerk (1798-1857), Vizepräsident der Mährischen Statthalterei and k.k. Hofrat, and Karoline (1820-1909), of the Wieser family. Coordinates mark the historic town centre; no birth house is identified in any source reached, and the parish registers were not consulted.
stops.campa: A son is born on the twelfth of February to Johann Karl Böhm, vice-president of the Moravian governorship, and his wife Karoline, born a Wieser. The house is a Habsburg official's house in Brünn, the German-speaking administrative capital of a Czech-speaking margraviate, a city of cloth mills and imperial paperwork. The boy is registered as Eugen Böhm. Later English reference works will move the birth to Vienna; the Biographical Dictionary, the Neue Deutsche Biographie and Brno's own municipal record all keep it here.
suggested_refs: The Brünn parish registers for February 1851, not consulted for this file
sources: encyklopedie.brna.cz, entry for Johann Karl Böhm

stops.name: Brünn, the predicate von Bawerk
stops.date_confidence: the ennoblement and the predicate are reported by Brno's municipal biographical encyclopedia as relayed in the dossier; that page was not independently refetched for this file, so the 1854 date is carried as reconstruction. The compound family name Böhm Ritter von Bawerk is confirmed by the NDB's form of the father's name. Month and day unknown, defaulted to 1 January.
stops.campa: Franz Joseph ennobles the senior Moravian official three years after the son is born, and Johann Karl Böhm takes the predicate von Bawerk. The family name becomes Böhm Ritter von Bawerk. It is service nobility, granted for administration rather than inherited from land or war, of the sort the monarchy manufactured by the hundred to bind its bureaucracy to the throne. The boy is three years old. His particle comes out of a state salary, and he keeps it for the rest of his life.
suggested_refs: The 1854 Adelsakt for Johann Karl Böhm in the Austrian State Archives, not consulted
sources: encyklopedie.brna.cz, entry for Johann Karl Böhm, as cited in the research dossier

stops.name: Vienna, the household after the father
stops.date_confidence: the father's death in 1857 is attested by the NDB, which gives his dates as 1798-1857. The removal of the family to Vienna is not documented in any source reached and is reconstructed from the fact that the son's schooling from the early 1860s is Viennese. Coordinates mark the inner city generally; no address is known. The mother's Wieser descent is stated by the NDB and makes the later Böhm-Bawerk / Wieser tie a blood relation, not only a school friendship.
stops.campa: Johann Karl dies in 1857 at fifty-nine. Karoline is thirty-seven, with children still to school, and the household moves to Vienna, where the gymnasia and the ministries are and where a Ritter's widow can place her sons. Her own people are the Wiesers, so the boy who will marry a Wieser and argue with a Wieser about the theory of value is already, at six, a Wieser cousin. No record reached names the quarter she took, and none says how a Ritter's widow's pension was reckoned in 1857.
suggested_refs: Viennese Meldezettel for the Böhm von Bawerk household in the later 1850s, not located
sources: Deutsche Biographie / NDB, deutsche-biographie.de/sfz4997.html (dates of both parents, Wieser descent)

stops.name: Vienna, the Schottengymnasium on the Freyung
stops.date_confidence: attested that both boys were pupils: the Schottengymnasium's own alumni roster lists Eugen Böhm von Bawerk (1851-1914) and Friedrich von Wieser (1851-1926), and de.wikipedia gives Wieser's birth as 10 July 1851 and his university entry as 1868, the same year as Böhm-Bawerk's. The 'friendly rivals for top marks' anecdote is traditional and rests on later retelling, not on school records. The date 1863 is a placeholder inside the gymnasium years, which no source reached dates individually. Coordinates corrected to Freyung 6.
stops.campa: At the Benedictine gymnasium on the Freyung he sits in the same rooms as Friedrich von Wieser, born the same year, and the two will matriculate at the same university in the same autumn. The school teaches Latin, Greek and the discipline of the Habsburg examination, and its alumni roster carries both names on the same page. Later accounts make them friendly rivals for the top marks. Neither of them has yet heard of a book called the Grundsätze, which will not be written for another eight years.
suggested_refs: The Schottengymnasium Jahresberichte for the 1860s, not consulted

stops.name: Vienna, law and the state sciences at the Alte Universität
stops.date_confidence: attested by ÖBL and en.wikipedia, which give 1868-1872 for the law and state-sciences course at Vienna. Month set to October to mark the start of the winter semester; no enrolment date was located. Coordinates corrected to the surveyed Alte Universität complex at Dr.-Ignaz-Seipel-Platz, 48.2088 / 16.3774, the same pin carl_menger.journey.json uses for that building.
stops.campa: He enrols in law and the state sciences at the University of Vienna, still housed in its eighteenth-century building beside the Jesuit church and not yet moved to the Ringstrasse palace it will occupy in his lifetime. The curriculum trains men for the civil service: Roman law, canon law, administration, finance. Political economy is a minor subject taught inside a law faculty by jurists. The faculty exists to produce officials for the imperial civil service. He takes four years over the course and leaves qualified as one.
suggested_refs: The Alte Universität complex on Dr.-Ignaz-Seipel-Platz, seat of the law faculty until the Ringstrasse move

segments.name: The Grundsätze and the German Tour

stops.name: Vienna, a book two students find for themselves
stops.date_confidence: the 1871 Vienna publication of Menger's Grundsätze der Volkswirthschaftslehre is attested and carries its own stop in carl_menger.journey.json at this identical pin, inherited here byte for byte. That Böhm-Bawerk read it as a student and turned to economics because of it is reconstruction: it is the standing account in the biographical literature and was not confirmed against a primary source for this file. Menger was not their examiner and is not recorded teaching them.
stops.campa: Carl Menger publishes the Grundsätze der Volkswirthschaftslehre in Vienna. Böhm-Bawerk and Wieser read it on their own account, outside any lecture course, and it turns both of them from law to economics. Menger never examines them; he encourages the private reading and later helps them to travel stipends instead. There is no chair, no seminar, no appointment. The lineage that will be called the Austrian School begins with two law students reading a book in their own time.
suggested_refs: Carl Menger, Grundsätze der Volkswirthschaftslehre (Vienna: Braumüller, 1871)
sources: carl_menger.journey.json (1871 Grundsätze stop, pin and publication)

stops.name: Vienna, the Finanzprokuratur and the doctorate
stops.date_confidence: attested: ÖBL and en.wikipedia converge on entry to the Lower Austrian financial administration in 1872 and on the Dr. jur. in 1875. The exact building is not confirmed; coordinates approximate the inner-city government quarter. Month and day unknown, defaulted to 1 January.
stops.campa: He enters the Lower Austrian Finanzprokuratur, the standard first post for a legally trained man of his class, and begins the civil-service career that will run beside the scholarship for the next forty-two years. The doctorate in law follows in 1875. From this year until his death he is almost never only an economist: an official who writes, later a professor who drafts legislation, later still a minister who publishes. Which of those he principally was is a question the record leaves open.
suggested_refs: The k.k. Finanzprokuratur für Niederösterreich, his first posting

stops.name: Heidelberg, the seminar of Karl Knies
stops.date_confidence: attested that he studied under Knies at Heidelberg on a postgraduate leave. The dossier's 'from 1875' is corrected: no source reached supports it. de.wikipedia dates the whole German tour 1876-1877 and the NDB calls it a two-year leave without giving years. The 1876 seminar manuscript on interest and its first English translation in 2023 are attested bibliographically. Coordinates corrected to the Alte Universität, Grabengasse 1, 49.4111 / 8.7061.
stops.campa: On leave from the ministry he goes to Heidelberg with Wieser and sits under Karl Knies, one of the three great names of the German Historical School. In Knies's seminar he drafts a paper on interest, on why a present good commands a premium over the same good a year hence. He does not publish it. The manuscript stays in his papers for a hundred and forty-seven years and is first put into English in 2023. Everything he writes afterwards is an answer to the question he sets himself here at twenty-five.
suggested_refs: Eugen von Böhm-Bawerk's Interest Theory of 1876, first English translation, 2023
sources: Bibliographical record of the 2023 translation of the 1876 manuscript

stops.name: Leipzig, Roscher and the comparative method
stops.date_confidence: attested that Leipzig under Roscher was the second station of the German tour. The individual leg dates vary by source; October 1876 is a placement inside the 1876-1877 window de.wikipedia gives, not a documented arrival. Coordinates mark the historic Augustusplatz university site; the specific 1870s lecture building was not confirmed.
stops.campa: The tour moves north to Leipzig and Wilhelm Roscher, who holds that economics is the comparative history of national economies and that laws abstracted out of history are a foreign habit imported from England. Böhm-Bawerk takes the method seriously enough to learn it thoroughly. Within a decade he will be on the other side of the Methodenstreit, defending Menger's deductive theory against exactly this school, with the advantage of having been taught by it in its own lecture rooms.
suggested_refs: Wilhelm Roscher's Leipzig lectures on the historical method

stops.name: Jena, the last of the three
stops.date_confidence: attested that Hildebrand at Jena was the third station; 1877 is the conventional placement and orders the segment rather than recording an arrival. Coordinates corrected: the Collegium Jenense is not on the Fürstengraben but stands between Teichgraben, Kollegiengasse, Leutragraben and Nonnenplan, at 50.9279 / 11.5844. The dossier's 50.9273 / 11.5893 is roughly 350 m east, at the separate Universitätshauptgebäude.
stops.campa: The last leg is Jena and Bruno Hildebrand, the third of the historical triumvirate and founder of the Jahrbücher für Nationalökonomie und Statistik. With him the young Austrian has now studied under all three of the men whose school he will spend his career opposing, and the three of them between them hold nearly everything the German profession then believes about how the subject should be done. He goes home to Vienna with a historian's training and a theorist's problem, and nothing published. Nine years later the Jahrbücher will print his own systematic statement of marginal utility.
suggested_refs: The Jahrbücher für Nationalökonomie und Statistik, founded by Hildebrand, later the vehicle of Böhm-Bawerk's 1886 paper

stops.name: Vienna, Privatdozent for political economy
stops.date_confidence: attested: en.wikipedia gives 1880 for the habilitation and the Privatdozent appointment at Vienna. Month and day unknown, defaulted to 1 January. The building is the Alte Universität, which the faculty still occupied; the Ringstrasse move comes later.
stops.campa: He habilitates in political economy at the university where he took his law degree and becomes Privatdozent, teaching without salary while the ministry keeps paying him. The thesis asks a lawyer's question in an economist's language: are legal rights and relations themselves economic goods, or only claims upon goods? Eight years in the Finanzprokuratur are good preparation for asking it. The monograph appears the following year with Wagner in Vienna.
suggested_refs: The Vienna law faculty habilitation records for 1880, not consulted

stops.name: Vienna, marriage to Paula Freiin von Wieser
stops.date_confidence: attested that the marriage took place in 1880 and that Paula was Friedrich von Wieser's sister; the description of it as close and childless comes from Carl Menger's 1915 memorial and from Schumpeter's biographical account, as cited in the secondary literature rather than read directly for this file. No church, no civil register entry and no date within the year was located. Coordinates mark inner Vienna generally.
stops.campa: He marries Paula Freiin von Wieser, Friedrich's sister. The schoolfellow becomes a brother-in-law. No church, no register entry and no wedding date beyond the year was found for this file. The two men who read the Grundsätze together will hold the two chairs that carry the school, dispute the theory of value in print, and be buried within twelve years of one another as its founders. Menger's 1915 memorial and Schumpeter's account both describe the marriage as close and childless.
suggested_refs: Carl Menger, memorial obituary, Almanach der Kaiserlichen Akademie der Wissenschaften in Wien (1915)
sources: Carl Menger's 1915 Academy memorial and Joseph Schumpeter's biographical essay, as cited in the secondary biographical literature

stops.name: Vienna, Rechte und Verhältnisse
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction as to the imprint: the 1881 Vienna (Wagner) publication is the standard bibliographical record and matches library catalogue entries, but no copy was inspected for this file. Month and day unknown, defaulted to 1 January.
stops.campa: The habilitation monograph appears: Rechte und Verhältnisse vom Standpunkte der volkswirthschaftlichen Güterlehre. It is his only sustained work of legal theory and the last time he writes chiefly as a jurist. What it establishes is a habit he never afterwards drops, of asking what a category actually consists of before asking what it does. Turned on capital eight years later, the same habit produces a book that half the economists of Europe spend forty years arguing with.
suggested_refs: Rechte und Verhältnisse vom Standpunkte der volkswirthschaftlichen Güterlehre (Vienna: Wagner, 1881)
sources: Standard bibliography of Böhm-Bawerk's works, matching WorldCat and library catalogue records

stops.name: Innsbruck, extraordinary professor in the Tyrol
stops.date_confidence: attested by ÖBL and en.wikipedia for the year 1881; the month is set to October for the winter semester and is not documented. Coordinates corrected: the dossier's 47.2653 / 11.3868 matches neither the 1881 site nor the modern one. In 1881-1889 the law faculty sat in the historic university quarter beside the Jesuitenkirche, 47.2684 / 11.3979; the Innrain 52 main building did not open until 1924.
stops.campa: He leaves Vienna for a small law faculty in the Tyrol, appointed extraordinary professor of political economy at Innsbruck. The faculty sits in the old university quarter beside the Jesuit church; the Innrain building the university uses now will not open for another forty-three years. He is thirty years old when he arrives. The teaching load is light and the town is small. He has eight uninterrupted years here, and in them he writes the two volumes that make his name.
suggested_refs: The old Innsbruck university quarter by the Jesuitenkirche, seat of the law faculty in the 1880s

stops.name: Innsbruck, a critical history of interest theories
stops.date_confidence: attested: the 1884 promotion to ordinary professor and the 1884 Innsbruck (Wagner) publication of Kapital und Kapitalzins, Erste Abtheilung, are given by ÖBL and en.wikipedia and match the standard bibliography. William Smart's English translation of 1890 is likewise attested. Month and day unknown, defaulted to 1 January.
stops.campa: Promoted to ordinary professor, he publishes the first half of Kapital und Kapitalzins: a critical history of every theory of interest anyone has yet proposed, from the canonists through the productivity theorists to the exploitation theorists. He clears the ground before he builds on it. William Smart's English translation follows in 1890 and puts the book in front of readers in Britain and America who have not previously thought of Vienna as a place where economics is done.
suggested_refs: Capital and Interest: A Critical History of Economical Theory, trans. William Smart (1890)

stops.name: Innsbruck, the Grundzüge in Hildebrand's journal
stops.date_confidence: attested: the paper appeared in the Jahrbücher für Nationalökonomie und Statistik, vol. 47 / new series 13, in 1886. Month and day unknown, defaulted to 1 January.
stops.campa: In Hildebrand's old journal he prints 'Grundzüge der Theorie des wirtschaftlichen Güterwerts,' the systematic Austrian statement of value, exchange and price, worked out from the wants of individual persons rather than from the cost of production. It is the paper that makes marginal utility teachable, and the one that fixes the Austrian vocabulary of want and satisfaction. He writes it in a provincial law faculty in the Tyrol, in a language most of the profession outside Austria and Germany does not read.
suggested_refs: Jahrbücher für Nationalökonomie und Statistik, vol. 47 (n.s. 13), 1886
sources: Journal citation, Jahrbücher für Nationalökonomie und Statistik vol. 47 / n.s. 13

stops.name: Innsbruck, the definition of capital left unsettled
stops.date_confidence: attested that Menger published Zur Theorie des Kapitals in 1888 disputing Böhm-Bawerk's definition of capital; carl_menger.journey.json carries the dispute as a stop of its own. The stop here is Böhm-Bawerk's, at his own Innsbruck desk, because the objection is aimed at the definition he is then writing on. Menger's private verdict is quoted from Schumpeter, History of Economic Analysis (1954), Part IV ch. 6, footnote, verified in the archive.org full text; the commonly cited page 847 n.8 could not be confirmed against a printed copy.
stops.campa: Menger publishes Zur Theorie des Kapitals in Vienna, disputing the definition his reader of 1871 is building on: whether capital is a stock of produced means of production, as Böhm-Bawerk holds, or a sum of money value awaiting employment. Neither man gives way and neither breaks with the other. Böhm-Bawerk goes on writing at Innsbruck with the objection standing. The school that will be named after the country keeps its two founding definitions of capital unreconciled to the end.
stops.quote: The time will come when people will realize that Böhm-Bawerk's theory is one of the greatest errors ever committed.
stops.quote_source: Carl Menger to Joseph Schumpeter, reported in Schumpeter, History of Economic Analysis (1954), Part IV ch. 6, footnote
suggested_refs: Carl Menger, Zur Theorie des Kapitals (1888)
sources: carl_menger.journey.json (1888 Zur Theorie des Kapitals stop)
Joseph A. Schumpeter, History of Economic Analysis (1954), archive.org identifier history-of-economic-analysis-joseph-a.-schumpeter

stops.name: Innsbruck, the positive theory
stops.date_confidence: attested: Kapital und Kapitalzins, Zweite Abtheilung: Positive Theorie des Capitals, Innsbruck (Wagner), 1889, with Smart's English translation in 1891. The quoted passage is from the Smart translation, Book III chapter IV, fetched from the text hosted at econlib.org. Month and day unknown, defaulted to 1 January.
stops.campa: The second half of Kapital und Kapitalzins appears: the positive theory. Production takes time; roundabout methods yield more but yield later; present goods therefore command a premium over future goods, and interest is that premium, an agio, not a payment for anything the capitalist does. To make the ranking of wants concrete he sets a farmer alone in the forest with five sacks of corn and follows him down to the last one. Smart's translation of 1891 carries the argument to Britain and America.
stops.quote: A colonial farmer, whose log hut stands by itself in the primeval forest, far away from the busy haunts of men, has just harvested five sacks of corn. These must serve him till the next autumn.
stops.quote_source: The Positive Theory of Capital, trans. William Smart (1891), Book III, chapter IV
suggested_refs: The Positive Theory of Capital, trans. William Smart (London: Macmillan, 1891)
sources: Smart translation text at econlib.org, Library of Economics and Liberty

stops.name: Vienna, back into the Finance Ministry
stops.date_confidence: attested by ÖBL and en.wikipedia that he resigned Innsbruck in 1889 and returned to the k.k. Finance Ministry, first as Ministerialrat and later as Sektionschef, working on direct-tax reform with Robert Meyer. Month set to October and not documented. Coordinates corrected: the ministry occupied the Winterpalais des Prinzen Eugen, Himmelpfortgasse 8, from 1848, at 48.2056 / 16.3728; the dossier's 48.2043 / 16.3746 is about 200 m southeast and its '4-8' address form is wrong.
stops.campa: He resigns the Innsbruck chair in the year the positive theory appears and comes back to the Finance Ministry in Prince Eugene's winter palace on the Himmelpfortgasse, first as Ministerialrat and then as Sektionschef. The task is direct-tax reform, stalled for a generation. He works on it with Robert Meyer, a subjectivist economist like himself, so that the Austrian income tax comes to be drafted by two men who hold that value is a matter of what individual people want.
suggested_refs: The Winterpalais des Prinzen Eugen, Himmelpfortgasse 8, seat of the k.k. Finance Ministry from 1848

stops.name: Vienna, the crown and the journal
stops.date_confidence: the 1892 founding of the Zeitschrift für Volkswirtschaft, Sozialpolitik und Verwaltung and his programmatic article 'Unsere Aufgaben' in its first number are attested. The vice-presidency of the currency-reform commission is reconstruction: it comes from a scholarly chronology relayed in the dossier and was not confirmed against any primary commission record for this file. Month and day unknown, defaulted to 1 January.
stops.campa: Austria-Hungary is moving off silver onto a gold-based crown, and he sits on the currency-reform commission that manages the change, one chronology naming him its vice-president. The same year he becomes a founding editor of the Zeitschrift für Volkswirtschaft, Sozialpolitik und Verwaltung and opens the first number with a piece called 'Unsere Aufgaben,' our tasks. Twenty-two years later the same journal will print the last two quarrels of his life.
suggested_refs: Zeitschrift für Volkswirtschaft, Sozialpolitik und Verwaltung, vol. 1 (1892), 'Unsere Aufgaben'
sources: Journal founding record and Böhm-Bawerk's 1892 article
Scholarly chronology of the 1892 Austrian currency commission, as relayed in the research dossier

stops.name: Vienna, finance minister in a caretaker cabinet
stops.date_confidence: attested that he held the finance portfolio in Kielmansegg's 1895 cabinet. The exact dates are flagged and not resolved: the dossier gives 19 June to 30 September 1895, while de.wikipedia gives the cabinet itself as 18 June to 2 October 1895. His personal swearing-in and resignation could differ from the cabinet's by days, and no source reached corroborates either personal date. The Grand Cross of the Order of Leopold and the rank of Wirklicher Geheimer Rat are reconstruction, from an Academy institutional page relayed in the dossier.
stops.campa: Kielmansegg forms a caretaker cabinet of officials in June and Böhm-Bawerk takes the finance portfolio for the first time. It is a government of civil servants assembled to hold the ground while the parties recover, and it lasts into the autumn without producing anything anyone can attribute to him personally. In the same year he receives the Grand Cross of the Order of Leopold and is made Wirklicher Geheimer Rat, which entitles the son of a Moravian bureaucrat to be addressed as Excellency. He is forty-four.
suggested_refs: The Kielmansegg cabinet of 1895, an interim government of officials
sources: Austrian Academy of Sciences institutional biography, oeaw.ac.at, as relayed in the dossier

stops.name: Vienna, the personal income tax of 1896
stops.date_confidence: attested: ÖBL credits him with drafting the personal-tax legislation of 1896, which introduced a general personal income tax with progressive rates in the Austrian half of the monarchy. Month and day of enactment not established here; defaulted to 1 January.
stops.campa: The direct-tax reform he was brought back for reaches the statute book: a general personal income tax with progressive rates, the first in the Austrian half of the monarchy, which the Biographical Dictionary credits him with drafting. The theorist of the agio on present goods spends his working days deciding what a household's present income is and what share of it the state may take. He is twenty-four years into the civil service and has published two of the most argued-over books on capital in Europe.
suggested_refs: The Austrian personal-tax legislation of 1896

stops.name: Vienna, the close of the Marxian system
stops.date_confidence: attested: 'Zum Abschluss des Marxschen Systems' appeared in Otto von Boenigk, ed., Staatswissenschaftliche Arbeiten: Festgaben für Karl Knies (1896), with Alice M. Macdonald's English translation in 1898. The quoted passage is at p. 64 of that translation, fetched from the archive.org full text, identifier karlmarxandclos00macdgoog. Month unknown; June is set to order the segment. Hilferding's 1904 reply and Sweezy's 1949 pairing are attested; the 'definitive destruction' framing is a later reception legend and is not stated here.
stops.campa: Out of office between cabinets, he writes the essay that will be reprinted longer than anything else he produced, for a Festschrift honouring his old Heidelberg teacher Knies. Marx's first volume has commodities exchanging at their labour values; the third, published posthumously two years earlier, has them exchanging at prices of production that differ from those values. Böhm-Bawerk says the second statement does not develop the first but cancels it.
stops.quote: I see here no explanation and reconciliation of a contradiction, but the bare contradiction itself.
stops.quote_source: Karl Marx and the Close of His System, trans. Alice M. Macdonald (1898), p. 64
suggested_refs: Rudolf Hilferding's 1904 reply, printed with Böhm-Bawerk's essay in Paul Sweezy's 1949 edition
sources: Böhm-Bawerk, Karl Marx and the Close of His System, trans. Macdonald (1898), archive.org identifier karlmarxandclos00macdgoog
Original publication in Boenigk, ed., Festgaben für Karl Knies (1896)

stops.name: Vienna, labour as one factor among several
stops.date_confidence: attested as to text: the quoted passage is at p. 80 of the Macdonald translation of 1898, fetched from archive.org, identifier karlmarxandclos00macdgoog. The date is an ordering device only: this is the second half of the same 1896 essay, not a separate publication, and is given its own stop because the argument is a distinct one. Whether the argument succeeds is a live dispute in the literature and is not adjudicated here.
stops.campa: The second half of the essay is not about a contradiction inside Marx but about the evidence for the labour theory itself. Prices do move with the labour expended when everything else is held still, Böhm-Bawerk grants, and that shows labour to be one determinant of price. It does not show it to be the only one, and the whole doctrine of surplus value rests on its being the only one. The controversy is not closed by this; Hilferding will answer in 1904, and the two texts are still printed together.
stops.quote: That in the case of 'other circumstances remaining equal' prices rise and fall according to the amount of labour expended proves clearly neither more nor less than that labour is one factor in determining prices.
stops.quote_source: Karl Marx and the Close of His System, trans. Alice M. Macdonald (1898), p. 80
suggested_refs: Paul Sweezy, ed., Karl Marx and the Close of His System / Böhm-Bawerk's Criticism of Marx (1949)
sources: Böhm-Bawerk, Karl Marx and the Close of His System, trans. Macdonald (1898), archive.org identifier karlmarxandclos00macdgoog

stops.name: Vienna, the embassy that is in no register
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction, and a negative one. The ambassadorship is unattested and is carried here as a documented error rather than as an event in his life. The 1920 Encyclopedia Americana is the earliest carrier traced; the claim was still present in the English Wikipedia text fetched during research ('1897: Ambassador to German court'). No Austrian career summary lists it: not ÖBL, not the NDB, not the University of Vienna, not the Academy. The stop sits at Vienna, not Berlin, because nothing places him in Berlin.
stops.campa: The 1920 Encyclopedia Americana states that between his first and second ministries he served as Austrian ambassador to the German court, and modern reference entries repeat it, one of them fetched during the research for this file. No Austrian career summary lists any diplomatic post: not the Biographical Dictionary, not the Neue Deutsche Biographie, not the university, not the Academy. Somewhere in the copying a Sektionschef of finance was made an envoy to Berlin. At what point, and out of what, nobody has traced.
suggested_refs: Encyclopedia Americana (1920), entry for Böhm-Bawerk, earliest traced carrier of the ambassadorship claim
sources: Österreichisches Biographisches Lexikon, 'Böhm-Bawerk, Eugen' (no diplomatic post listed)

stops.name: Vienna, finance minister under Gautsch
stops.date_confidence: attested by ÖBL and en.wikipedia: 30 November 1897 to 5 March 1898, in Paul Gautsch von Frankenthurn's first cabinet, formed in the crisis that followed the Badeni language ordinances.
stops.campa: Badeni's language ordinances have brought the Reichsrat to a standstill and the German-speaking cities to riot. Badeni falls, Gautsch forms a cabinet, and Böhm-Bawerk takes the finance ministry a second time. It lasts ninety-five days. He is a technician of budgets handed a portfolio in a constitutional crisis over which language a Bohemian official must be able to write, and the ministry ends in March with neither the crisis nor the budget settled.
suggested_refs: The Badeni language ordinances of 1897 and the parliamentary crisis they touched off

stops.name: Vienna, the Administrative Court in the Palais Porcia
stops.date_confidence: the office is attested; the start year is not. ÖBL gives only 'Senatspräsident am Verwaltungsgerichtshof bis 1900', an end date, and neither Wikipedia supplies a start. 1898 is the conventional placement and orders the segment only. The venue is corrected: per Wien Geschichte Wiki the court sat at Weihburggasse 22 from 1876 and moved on 1 May 1882 into the Palais Porcia, Herrengasse 23, where it stayed until 1902. It was never in the Justizpalast, where the dossier had placed it, and its Judenplatz seat dates only from 2013.
stops.campa: Out of the cabinet, he is made a senate president at the Imperial Administrative Court, which has sat since 1882 in the Palais Porcia in the Herrengasse and will move out in 1902. He hears appeals brought against the administration, which is to say against the machinery he has spent his working life inside. He holds the post until 1900, alongside the seat in the upper house he receives in 1899. It is the only judicial office of his career, and no source reached for this file records a single one of his judgments.
suggested_refs: The Palais Porcia, Herrengasse 23, seat of the k.k. Verwaltungsgerichtshof 1882-1902

stops.name: Vienna, a seat for life in the Herrenhaus
stops.date_confidence: attested by ÖBL and cross-referenced with en.wikipedia for the elevation to the upper chamber in 1899; September is given in the dossier's institutional record. Day unknown, defaulted to 01. Coordinates mark the Reichsrat building on the Ring.
stops.campa: The emperor appoints him for life to the Herrenhaus, the upper chamber of the Reichsrat, where the members sit by birth, by office or by imperial nomination and never by any vote. He stands for nothing, builds no faction, and leaves no trace of a party machine. It is the standard Habsburg promotion of a senior official into the house that reviews his own department's bills. He is forty-eight, and he keeps the seat for the last fifteen years of his life.
suggested_refs: The Herrenhaus of the Austrian Reichsrat, appointed chamber of the monarchy

segments.name: The Third Ministry and the Army Estimates

stops.name: Vienna, the long ministry
stops.date_confidence: attested that he served as finance minister from 1900 to 1904 and that the term is associated with Koerber's government. The start date is flagged and not resolved: de.wikipedia dates Koerber's first cabinet from 19 January 1900, with Wittek's caretaker cabinet running to 18 January, so a strict 18 January appointment would fall in the transition rather than under Koerber. Gerschenkron's reading of the fiscal conflict is a scholarly assessment, not a contemporary document.
stops.campa: He is appointed finance minister a third time and holds the office nearly five years, longer than the two earlier terms together. Koerber wants railways and a canal network built on borrowed money; Böhm-Bawerk wants a balanced budget and the gold standard defended. The conflict runs the whole length of the ministry. His admirers will call it principled restraint, and Alexander Gerschenkron will call it the obstruction of a backward economy's one chance at investment.
suggested_refs: Alexander Gerschenkron's assessment of the Koerber programme and its fiscal opposition

stops.name: Vienna, elected into the Academy
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The 1900 corresponding election and the 1902 full membership come from an Austrian Academy institutional biography relayed in the dossier and were not refetched from an Academy roster for this file. Month unknown, set to May to order the segment. Coordinates corrected: the Academy occupies the Neue Aula on Dr.-Ignaz-Seipel-Platz 2, part of the Alte Universität complex whose surveyed pin is 48.2088 / 16.3774; the dossier's 48.2103 / 16.3779 sits north of the square.
stops.campa: The Imperial Academy of Sciences elects him a corresponding member, and two years later a full one, in the middle of the ministry that will occupy him until 1904. The building is the Neue Aula of the old university, a hundred paces from the rooms where he read Roman law as a boy of seventeen in 1868, and across the square from the lecture halls where he habilitated in 1880. He will be its vice-president in 1907 and its president in 1911, and he will hold that last office until he dies.
suggested_refs: The Neue Aula on Dr.-Ignaz-Seipel-Platz, seat of the Kaiserliche Akademie der Wissenschaften
sources: Austrian Academy of Sciences institutional biography, oeaw.ac.at/175-jahre/personen/tafel, as relayed in the dossier

stops.name: Vienna, the Brussels Sugar Convention implemented from a desk
stops.date_confidence: attested that the Brussels Sugar Convention was signed on 5 March 1902 and that Böhm-Bawerk was the responsible Austrian minister for its implementation. No evidence was found that he travelled to Brussels; the stop is therefore placed at the ministry in Vienna. The popular account that he single-handedly ended a two-hundred-year bounty is a compression and is not repeated as fact.
stops.campa: The powers sign at Brussels on the fifth of March an agreement to abolish the export bounties that have made European sugar cheap in London and dear at home. Böhm-Bawerk implements it for Austria from the Himmelpfortgasse. He does not travel to Brussels, and nothing reached for this file puts him in the room. The popular telling credits one Austrian minister with ending a two-hundred-year subsidy single-handed. The treaty was multilateral, the negotiation belonged to the foreign ministry, and the abolition took a legislative session.
suggested_refs: The Brussels Sugar Convention of 5 March 1902 and its Austrian implementing legislation
sources: Treaty record of the Brussels Sugar Convention, 1902
Contemporaneous Austrian fiscal-policy analysis cited in the scholarly literature

stops.name: Vienna, out of the ministry for good
stops.date_confidence: attested that he left the finance ministry on 26 October 1904 and took a university chair. The army-budget explanation comes from later accounts rather than from a contemporary document and is reconstruction. No investigation naming him as an accuser of criminal conduct was found; that version of the story is not supported by anything reached.
stops.campa: He leaves the finance ministry on the twenty-sixth of October, formally in order to take a university chair. The accounts that follow add that the army's rising demands, and defence estimates he judged insufficiently transparent, had made the balanced budget he defended for five years impossible to hold. He accuses no one of anything criminal and no investigation names him. He is fifty-three, and for the first time since 1872 he is not a servant of the Austrian state.
suggested_refs: The Austrian defence estimates of 1904 and the fall of the Koerber finance ministry
sources: University of Vienna career record, as cited in the research dossier

segments.name: The Seminar in the Ringstrasse Palace

stops.name: Vienna, the chair of political economy
stops.date_confidence: attested: en.wikipedia gives 1904-1914 as full professor of political economy at the University of Vienna, matching ÖBL. Month set to November, immediately after the 26 October resignation, and not separately documented. Pin inherited from carl_menger.journey.json for the Ringstrasse main building.
stops.campa: He takes a chair at the University of Vienna, now in its Ringstrasse palace, thirty-six years after enrolling in the old building down by the Jesuit church. The man who arrives is not a returning academic. He is an Excellency, three times finance minister, a senate president of the Administrative Court, a life member of the upper house, and within seven years the president of the Academy. He has not held a university post in fifteen years. He teaches for ten more and dies in post.
suggested_refs: The University of Vienna main building on the Ringstrasse, occupied from 1884

stops.name: Vienna, four men at one table
stops.date_confidence: attested that the private seminar ran from October 1904 to 1914 and that Mises, Schumpeter, Otto Bauer and Rudolf Hilferding took part; ludwig_von_mises.journey.json carries its own stop for it, whose pin is inherited here byte for byte. The date 1905 orders the segment; the seminar has no single date. Enrolment evidence is uneven for other names popularly attached to it, and 'student' there can mean registered pupil, visitor or later follower. The quoted fragment is Mises's, cited to his Notes and Recollections through that file.
stops.campa: The private seminar he runs in these rooms puts Ludwig von Mises, Joseph Schumpeter, Otto Bauer and Rudolf Hilferding around one table: the two who will carry Austrian economics into the next century and the two who will build Austro-Marxism against it. Hilferding has already answered Böhm-Bawerk's attack on Marx in print. Bauer will lead a party and a republic. They argue with each other in the room instead of seceding from it, and their teacher chairs the argument.
stops.quote: a chairman who occasionally also participated in the discussion
stops.quote_source: Ludwig von Mises, Notes and Recollections, on Böhm-Bawerk's Vienna seminar, as cited in ludwig_von_mises.journey.json
suggested_refs: Ludwig von Mises, Notes and Recollections, on the Böhm-Bawerk seminar
sources: ludwig_von_mises.journey.json (seminar stop, pin, and Mises quote)

stops.name: Vienna, vice-president of the Academy
stops.date_confidence: attested by ÖBL and en.wikipedia, both giving 1907-1911. An Academy display page carries the year as 1807, a typographical error corrected by the near-contemporary record and by the plain sequence of his career. Month and day unknown, defaulted to 1 January.
stops.campa: He is elected vice-president of the Imperial Academy of Sciences and holds the office four years. One of the Academy's own display pages gives the date as 1807, a century early, which would have put him in the chair forty-four years before he was born. The near-contemporary record and the plain sequence of his career fix it at 1907. So does Menger's memorial of 1915, written by the man who had spent twenty years disputing his definition of capital.
suggested_refs: Carl Menger's 1915 Academy memorial, which fixes the vice-presidency at 1907
sources: Austrian Academy of Sciences institutional biography, oeaw.ac.at

stops.name: Vienna, a hundred thousand crowns
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The donation and its amount come from an Austrian Academy institutional record relayed in the dossier; no primary Academy donation register was reached for this file. Where the money came from is not stated in anything reached and is left open here rather than guessed at. Month and day unknown, defaulted to 1 January.
stops.campa: He gives the Academy a hundred thousand crowns. It is a large sum, several times a Sektionschef's annual salary, and nothing in the record says where it came from: family money, the Wieser connection, a lifetime of ministerial pay, investments nobody itemised. The man who wrote three volumes on the origin of interest, and who spent nine years deciding what the Austrian state might take out of a household's income, leaves no account at all of the origin of his own capital. The Academy, receiving it, appears not to have asked.
suggested_refs: The Academy's donation records for 1908, not consulted
sources: Austrian Academy of Sciences institutional record, as relayed in the research dossier

stops.name: Vienna, president of the Imperial Academy
stops.date_confidence: attested by ÖBL and en.wikipedia, both giving 1911-1914 for the presidency. Month and day unknown, defaulted to 1 January.
stops.campa: He is elected president of the Imperial Academy of Sciences and will hold the office until he dies. The Academy is the senior scientific body of the monarchy and its presidency is the last rung of a ladder he stepped onto in 1872 as a junior official in the Lower Austrian financial administration. He runs it for three years from an office in a building where he once sat law examinations, and holds the chair and the seat in the upper house at the same time.
suggested_refs: The Kaiserliche Akademie der Wissenschaften in Wien, presidency 1911-1914

stops.name: Vienna, elected to the Lincei without leaving the city
stops.date_confidence: attested: de.wikipedia states directly that he was elected a foreign member of the Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei in 1911, and ÖBL lists his degrees as Dr. jur. (Wien) and Dr. phil. h.c. (Heidelberg). The dossier's 'class of moral sciences' detail is unverified and is not repeated. Month unknown, set to June to order the segment. The stop sits at his own Vienna pin because no travel to Rome is documented anywhere reached.
stops.campa: Rome's Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei elects him a foreign member. He does not go to Rome; nothing reached for this file puts him in Italy at all. Heidelberg has already given him an honorary doctorate in philosophy, thirty-five years after he sat in Knies's seminar there as a visiting Austrian official on ministry leave. Apart from those two years in German lecture rooms in his twenties, he has lived his whole life between Vienna and the Tyrol. The honours arrive by post.
suggested_refs: The membership rolls of the Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei for 1911, not consulted directly

stops.name: Vienna, against his own student
stops.date_confidence: attested: 'Eine dynamische Theorie des Kapitalzinses' appeared in the Zeitschrift für Volkswirtschaft, Sozialpolitik und Verwaltung, vol. 22 (1913). Month and day unknown, defaulted to 1 January. That Schumpeter had sat in the seminar is attested through ludwig_von_mises.journey.json and the standard intellectual histories.
stops.campa: Schumpeter, who sat in his seminar, has built a theory in which interest arises out of development, out of the entrepreneur's disturbance of a stationary economy, and not out of any premium on present goods. Böhm-Bawerk gives an article in his own journal to taking it apart, and calls the dynamic theory of interest by its name in the title so that nobody can mistake the target. Teacher and pupil conduct the quarrel in print, in public, in a periodical the teacher edits and the pupil publishes in. They never agree about where interest comes from.
suggested_refs: Zeitschrift für Volkswirtschaft, Sozialpolitik und Verwaltung, vol. 22 (1913)
sources: Journal citation, Zeitschrift für Volkswirtschaft, Sozialpolitik und Verwaltung, vol. 22 (1913)

stops.name: Vienna, three mornings in the Neue Freie Presse
stops.date_confidence: attested: the three-part article ran in the Neue Freie Presse on 6, 8 and 9 January 1914 and was reprinted in Gesammelte Schriften vol. I, pp. 497-515. Coordinates corrected: Wien Geschichte Wiki gives the paper's editorial address as 1., Fichtegasse 9-11, and the street runs at about 48.2028 / 16.3752; the dossier's 48.2037 / 16.3745 is roughly 120 m north.
stops.campa: On the sixth, the eighth and the ninth of January the Neue Freie Presse prints a three-part article by him on Austria's trade balance. An excess of imports over exports, he argues, is not by itself proof that a country is being made poorer, and the thing actually worth alarm is the direction of Austrian public spending. It is the last thing he publishes. Seven months later the state whose budgets he had guarded for five years goes to war on credit.
suggested_refs: 'Unsere passive Handelsbilanz,' Neue Freie Presse, 6, 8 and 9 January 1914, reprinted in Gesammelte Schriften I, 497-515
sources: Wien Geschichte Wiki, Neue Freie Presse and Fichtegasse

stops.name: Vienna, power or economic law
stops.date_confidence: attested: 'Macht oder ökonomisches Gesetz?' appeared in the Zeitschrift für Volkswirtschaft, Sozialpolitik und Verwaltung, vol. 23, pp. 205-271, in 1914. Month unknown; June is set to place it before the death in August and to order the segment.
stops.campa: His last theoretical essay asks whether organised power can override economic law: whether a cartel, a union or a state can simply decree a price or a wage and have it hold. His answer is that coercion works inside the constraints of scarcity, demand and supply rather than outside them, and does not abolish them. He does not deny that power shapes a bargain; he denies that it can suspend the arithmetic. The essay runs to sixty-six pages in the journal he founded, and it is printed in the summer of 1914.
suggested_refs: Zeitschrift für Volkswirtschaft, Sozialpolitik und Verwaltung, vol. 23 (1914), 205-271
sources: Journal citation, Zeitschrift für Volkswirtschaft, Sozialpolitik und Verwaltung, vol. 23 (1914)

stops.name: Kramsach, the death in the Inn valley
stops.date_confidence: attested: ÖBL gives 'gest. Kramsach bei Brixlegg, 27.8.1914', confirmed independently by both Wikipedias. Coordinates corrected: Kramsach is 47.4447 / 11.8814; the dossier's two lenses gave 47.4514 / 11.9122 and 47.4667 / 11.9000, disagreeing with each other by about 2.5 km and both wrong. The venous thrombosis attributed to Menger's 1915 Almanach obituary could not be verified in any source reached and is not stated here. The exact house or sanatorium was not located.
stops.campa: He dies on holiday in the Inn valley below Brixlegg, on the twenty-seventh of August, aged sixty-three. The war is three weeks old and the empire has already begun the borrowing he spent a career refusing. A few catalogues put the death in Vienna; the Biographical Dictionary, the university and the Academy all say Kramsach. Carl Menger, who disputed his definition of capital in 1888 and outlived him by seven years, writes the memorial for the Academy he was still presiding over.
suggested_refs: Carl Menger, obituary, Almanach der Kaiserlichen Akademie der Wissenschaften in Wien (1915)

segments.name: The Grave, the Courtyard, the Banknote

stops.name: Vienna, Zentralfriedhof, group 32A, number 52
stops.date_confidence: the grave is attested: de.wikipedia and Wien Geschichte Wiki both give Ehrengrab, Gruppe 32 A, Nummer 52, and de.wikipedia carries a photograph of the stone. The date is flagged: the dossier's 'reinterred November 1915' is not in the cited article, which gives group and number with no burial or reinterment date at all, so the year here orders the segment only and the November 1915 reinterment is not repeated as fact. The Ehrengrab's current administrative renewal status could not be confirmed; the Friedhöfe Wien grave-search URL attempted returned 404. Pin inherited byte for byte from carl_menger.journey.json; the dossier's 16.4494 lies well east of the honorary-grave core.
stops.campa: He is laid in an honorary grave at the Central Cemetery, group 32A, number 52, in the block the city keeps beside the main avenue for people it does not intend to forget. Menger will be buried in the same ground in 1921, group zero, row one, number eighty-eight, nearer the gate on the Simmeringer Hauptstrasse. By 1921 the empire whose finances he ran three times no longer exists. The two men who never settled between them what capital is lie a few hundred metres apart.
suggested_refs: The Ehrengrab register of the Wiener Zentralfriedhof, group 32A
sources: Wien Geschichte Wiki, Eugen Böhm von Bawerk
carl_menger.journey.json (Menger's own grave stop and pin)

stops.name: Vienna, the bronze in the Arkadenhof
stops.date_confidence: attested, and upgraded from the dossier's flag: Wien Geschichte Wiki's 'Böhm-Bawerk-Denkmal' entry places the memorial at 1., Universitätsring 1, in the University of Vienna's Arkadenhof, created 1950, unveiled 23 June 1950, by E. Delug, and records it as still extant. The dossier had carried this as unconfirmed. Pin is the university's Ringstrasse building, inherited from carl_menger.journey.json.
stops.campa: The University of Vienna unveils a memorial to him in the arcaded courtyard on the twenty-third of June, among the busts and plaques of the professors the faculty chooses to keep in front of itself. It is thirty-six years after his death, in a city still under four-power occupation, in a republic that lost the currency he helped put onto gold and has had a schilling again for only five years. The address is Universitätsring 1. The work is by E. Delug. It is still there.
suggested_refs: Wien Geschichte Wiki, 'Böhm-Bawerk-Denkmal,' Universitätsring 1, Arkadenhof
sources: Wien Geschichte Wiki, Böhm-Bawerk-Denkmal (creation 1950, unveiling 23 June 1950, sculptor E. Delug)

stops.name: Vienna, the last hundred-schilling note
stops.date_confidence: attested in outline: en.wikipedia states that his image appeared on the hundred-schilling banknote from 1984 until the euro was introduced in 2002. The precise dates relayed in the dossier, designed 2 January 1984, issued 14 October 1985, withdrawn as legal tender 28 February 2002, rest on the dossier plus that looser summary; the OeNB's own banknote-history page was fetched and did not surface this note's text in the excerpt retrieved. Pin is the Academy building shown on the reverse, not a bank office.
stops.campa: The Austrian National Bank puts his portrait on a hundred-schilling note, his face on the front and on the back the Academy of Sciences he presided over. It is the last hundred-schilling note the republic issues. The design is dated January 1984, the note goes into circulation in October 1985, and it stops being legal tender at the end of February 2002, when the schilling gives way to the euro. The building on the reverse is the Neue Aula, where he was elected in 1900.
suggested_refs: The 1985 Austrian 100-schilling banknote, obverse Böhm-Bawerk, reverse the Academy of Sciences
sources: Numismatic detail relayed in the research dossier; OeNB banknote-history page fetched without confirming text
